title: Sparkling, fortified, sweet, beer, sake and spirits
lead: Everything outside still wine, at Advanced depth: the laws that define each drink, the age ladders, and the production choices you can taste.

intro.title: WHERE THE LAW DRAWS THE LINE
intro.text: Most Advanced questions here are a number set by law. Learn which measure each drink is judged by.

sections.name: Sparkling methods and Champagne law
sections.source: Comité Champagne (making-process and label fact sheets; AOC cahier des charges); EU Regulation 1308/2013; eCFR 27 CFR 4.21 and 4.24; VQA Ontario

lines.label: Pressure sets the category
lines.text: EU law: semi-sparkling 1 to 2.5 bar, sparkling 3 bar or more, quality sparkling 3.5 bar or more, at 20 °C. Champagne sits at about 6 bar.

lines.label: Champagne's rulebook
lines.text: Seven main grapes, 102 liters of juice per 160 kg, tirage only from January 1 after harvest, and 12 months on the lees before disgorging.

know: A 4,000 kg press load (marc) gives 2,050 L of cuvée and 500 L of taille, kept apart.
Beyond Chardonnay, Meunier and Pinot Noir, the rules allow Arbane, Petit Meslier, Pinot Blanc and Pinot Gris; Voltis is capped at 10% of a blend.
Rosé Champagne may be a blend of white and red wine made before tirage, or made by maceration or saignée.
Label codes: RM grower, NM merchant house, CM cooperative, RC co-op member's own label, ND distributor, MA private label.
In U.S. law Champagne is semi-generic; a tank-fermented 'champagne' must add words like 'bulk process'.

sections.name: Sherry and Port
sections.source: Consejo Regulador Jerez-Xérès-Sherry (sherry.wine); Instituto dos Vinhos do Douro e do Porto (ivdp.pt)

lines.label: Sherry
lines.text: Ten towns hold DO vineyards, from Jerez to Lebrija in Seville province. Age-certified Sherry: VOS (20+ years) and VORS (30+), plus 12- and 15-year indications and sealed-cask añadas.

lines.label: Port
lines.text: Usually one part grape spirit to four parts must-wine, landing at 19-22% ABV. LBV gets four to six years in wood; Vintage is bottled two to three years after harvest.

know: VOS/VORS are certified lot by lot by an independent panel, and only for Amontillado, Oloroso, Palo Cortado or Pedro Ximénez.
For each liter of VOS sold, 20 must stay in the solera; for VORS, 30.
Flor weakens after about seven or eight years, so very old Sherries are mostly oxidative.
A pago name such as Macharnudo or Balbaína needs 85% of the grapes from that pago.
Crusted Port stays in bottle at least 3 years before sale; Colheita ages at least 7 years in cask.

sections.name: Madeira, Marsala, VDN and VDL
sections.source: Wine Folly (Madeira); Marsala DOC disciplinare (Italian Ministry of Agriculture); INAO (AOP Maury); Pineau des Charentes cahier des charges; EU Regulation 1308/2013

lines.label: Madeira and Marsala
lines.text: Madeira climbs from Rainwater (3 years) to 5, 10, 15 and 20+ years, Colheita (5) and Frasqueira (20 in canteiro). Marsala: Fine 1, Superiore 2, Superiore Riserva 4, Vergine 5, Vergine Stravecchio 10.

lines.label: VDN and VDL
lines.text: A vin doux naturel is muted partway through fermentation with 96% grape spirit, as in Maury. A vin de liqueur is must muted with spirit, as Pineau des Charentes is with Cognac.

know: Marsala Oro and Ambra use Grillo, Catarratto, Inzolia and Damaschino; Rubino uses Perricone, Nero d'Avola and Nerello Mascalese.
Mosto cotto is banned in Marsala Vergine and in Oro and Rubino Fine and Superiore; Ambra may use it.
Marsala sweetness: secco under 40 g/L, semisecco 40-100 g/L, dolce over 100 g/L.
Maury: Grenache Noir is the base of grenat and tuilé; ambré and tuilé age oxidatively, sometimes for decades.
Pineau des Charentes: 16-22% ABV; white ages at least 18 months (12 in oak), red and rosé 12 (8 in oak).

sections.name: Sweet and aromatized wines
sections.source: VQA Ontario; eCFR 27 CFR 4.21 and 4.24; Wines of South Africa; Sherry Council (Pedro Ximénez); EU Regulation 251/2014

lines.label: Sweet by method
lines.text: From Level 2: noble rot, drying, freezing and fortifying. Ontario's VQA law shows the ripeness ladder: Late Harvest 22° Brix, Select 26°, Special Select 30°, Icewine 35°.

lines.label: Aromatized
lines.text: EU law: an aromatized wine is at least 75% wine, 14.5% to under 22% ABV. Vermouth tastes of Artemisia (wormwood); Quinquina of quinine; Americano of wormwood and gentian.

know: VQA allows 'Appassimento' or 'Vin de Cure' for wines of at least 85% dried grapes.
Pedro Ximénez grapes are sun-dried (asoleo) before pressing; the wine is served at 12-14 °C.
Constantia's dessert wines were famous across Europe in the 18th century.
In U.S. law, dessert wine means over 14% and up to 24% ABV, and Vermouth is a generic name.
'Sangría' as a sales name is reserved for Spain and Portugal; egg-based aromatized wine needs at least 10 g of egg yolk per liter.

sections.name: Beer and sake
sections.source: BJCP 2021 Style Guidelines; International Trappist Association; National Tax Agency of Japan; National Research Institute of Brewing (NRIB)

lines.label: Classic beers
lines.text: Know each by place and method: Brussels-area lambic is spontaneously fermented in old oak; gueuze blends one-, two- and three-year-old lambic; Berliner Weisse sours with lactic bacteria.

lines.label: Sake law
lines.text: Japan's National Tax Agency sets eight special designations by polishing ratio, koji share and added alcohol. Every one needs at least 15% koji rice.

know: Weissbier: malted wheat is at least half the grist; banana-and-clove yeast; decoction mash is traditional.
Westmalle popularized the Tripel in 1931; an Authentic Trappist Product is made at the abbey, under the monks or nuns.
Junmai lost its 70% polishing rule in 2004; Honjozo is 70% or less, Ginjo 60%, Daiginjo 50%.
Added brewer's alcohol in Ginjo or Honjozo is capped at 10% of the white rice weight.
Kimoto and yamahai grow lactic bacteria for the seed mash; sokujo adds lactic acid and saves about two weeks.

sections.name: Spirits: distillation, aging laws, aperitifs and digestifs
sections.source: EU Regulation 2019/787; Scotch Whisky Regulations 2009; eCFR 27 CFR part 5; Bureau National Interprofessionnel du Cognac

lines.label: Distillation
lines.text: Distilling below a set strength keeps the raw material's taste: EU and Scotch whisky under 94.8% ABV, bourbon at 160 proof or less. Single Malt Scotch uses pot stills; Cognac is distilled twice in a Charentais still.

lines.label: Aging laws
lines.text: Scotch: 3 years in Scotland, in oak casks of 700 L or less; EU brandy: 1 year in big oak or 6 months in casks under 1,000 L. Cognac: VS 2, VSOP 4, XO 10 years.

know: Straight whiskey rests at least 2 years in charred new oak, entered at 125 proof or less.
Bottled in bond: one season, one distiller, one distillery, at least 4 years in wood, bottled at 100 proof.
Scotch protects two localities (Campbeltown, Islay) and three regions (Highland, Lowland, Speyside).
Base materials by law: rum from sugar cane, Scotch from malted barley (other whole grains allowed), brandy from wine spirit, agave spirits 51%+ agave.
EU aperitif and digestif rules: liqueur 100 g/L sugar and 15% ABV; crème de 250 g/L; bitter 15% ABV.

visuals.note: Age statements count the youngest spirit in the blend.

mixups.why: VOS certifies over 20 years; VORS over 30 years.
A VDN ferments partway before muting; a VDL is must muted with spirit, like Pineau with Cognac.
Vermouth's taste comes from Artemisia (wormwood); Quinquina's from quinine.
Namazake is never pasteurized; nama-chozo is pasteurized once, at bottling.

facts.fact: EU Regulation 1308/2013 Annex VII Part II: sparkling wine has an excess pressure of not less than 3 bar at 20 °C; quality sparkling wine not less than 3.5 bar; semi-sparkling wine not less than 1 bar and not more than 2.5 bar; aerated versions get their CO2 wholly or partly added.

Comité Champagne fact sheet: pressing unit (marc) = 4,000 kg of grapes, pressed whole-bunch and slowly with separate fractions; cuvée 2,050 L; taille 500 L; second fermentation pressure 6 bar at 20 °C; non-vintage 15 months minimum, vintage 36 months minimum; 1.2 kg of grapes = 1 bottle.

Champagne cahier des charges: AOC Champagne is reserved for white or rosé sparkling wines; main varieties are Arbane, Chardonnay, Meunier, Petit Meslier, Pinot Blanc, Pinot Gris and Pinot Noir, plus Voltis as an adaptation variety (at most 5% of plantings and 10% of a blend; main varieties at least 90% of the blend).

Champagne cahier des charges: at most 102 liters of settled must per 160 kg of grapes; rosé may be made by direct pressing, maceration or saignée, or by blending white and red wines before tirage; second fermentation only in glass bottles; tirage not before January 1 after the harvest; disgorgement not before twelve months after tirage.

Comité Champagne label guide: professional registration codes RM (récoltant manipulant, grower producer), NM (négociant manipulant, merchant producer), CM (coopérative de manipulation), RC (récoltant coopérateur, cooperative members selling under their own label), ND (négociant distributeur), MA (marque d'acheteur, private label); Extra Brut < 6 g/L, Brut < 12 g/L.

27 CFR 4.21(b): sparkling grape wine gets its CO2 solely from fermentation in a closed container; 'champagne' (as a TTB type) has its secondary fermentation in glass containers of not more than one gallon; other champagne-style wines must add terms such as 'bulk process' or 'fermented outside the bottle'; 'charmat method' may be added.
27 CFR 4.24(b)(2): Champagne is listed as a semi-generic name in U.S. law, usable only with the true origin.
VQA Ontario: sparkling wine has undergone secondary fermentation in tank or bottle with a pressure of not less than 300 kPa; artificial carbonation is prohibited.

Sherry Council: in 2000 the Consejo Regulador created two certified-age categories: VOS (Vinum Optimum Signatum, Very Old Sherry, over 20 years) and VORS (Vinum Optimum Rare Signatum, Very Old Rare Sherry, over 30 years); certification is per saca (lot), judged by an independent tasting committee; certified-age wines must be Amontillado, Oloroso, Palo Cortado or Pedro Ximénez.

Sherry Council: for every liter of VOS sold at least 20 liters must remain in the aging system (30 for VORS); 12- and 15-year indications certify the whole solera, with sales quotas of one-twelfth and one-fifteenth; añadas (vintage Sherries) age statically in casks sealed by the Consejo.
Sherry Council: after an average of seven or eight years the flor weakens, so very old Sherries are mostly oxidatively aged.
Sherry Council: ten towns have DO vineyards, including Jerez de la Frontera, El Puerto de Santa María, Sanlúcar de Barrameda and Lebrija (in Seville province); Chipiona is home to Moscatel.
Sherry Council: the official pago map was completed in 2015; a pago name (e.g. Macharnudo, Balbaína, Añina, Carrascal) may be used with at least 85 percent of the grapes from that pago.
Sherry Council: Pedro Ximénez comes from sun-dried grapes (asoleo); fermentation is stopped by adding wine alcohol; aging is exclusively oxidative; serve at 12-14 °C.
Sherry Council: Generoso Liqueur Wines are blends (cabeceo) of Generoso wines with naturally sweet wines or concentrated must, always over 5 g/L of sugar.
Sherry Council: Pale Cream is biologically aged wine (Fino or Manzanilla) sweetened with rectified concentrated must to keep its pale color; it entered the DO rules in the 1960s.

IVDP: the usual proportion is one part grape spirit to four parts must-wine, giving 19-22% ABV with residual sweetness; grapes are trodden in lagares or processed by modern methods; wines age in the Douro or in Vila Nova de Gaia lodges.
IVDP: White Port sweetness styles run extra dry, dry, semi-sweet, sweet, very sweet and Lágrima.

IVDP: Vintage Port is from a single year, bottled two to three years after the vintage, and develops 10 to 50 years in bottle; LBV is a single-year Ruby aged four to six years in wood; Crusted must be kept in bottle at least three years before sale; Colheita is a single-vintage Tawny aged at least seven years in cask; White Port may carry 10, 20, 30 or 40 Years.

Wine Folly: Madeira categories: Rainwater (3-year aging requirement); 5 Years/Reserve; 10 Years/Special Reserve; 15 Years/Extra Reserve; 20, 30, 40, 50+ Years; Colheita (single vintage, at least 5 years before release); Frasqueira (single vintage, at least 20 years in canteiro).

Wine Folly: in the estufa method wine is heated in stainless steel tanks for about 3 months, up to 50 °C; canteiro casks age at least 2 years in warm lofts; Tinta Negra is used mostly in Rainwater; Sercial is driest and Malvasia (Malmsey) sweetest; an opened bottle keeps about 6 months.

Marsala DOC disciplinare: Fine 1 year minimum aging, 17.5% total alcohol; Superiore 2 years, 18%; Superiore Riserva 4 years; Vergine (Soleras) 5 years, 18%; Vergine Stravecchio (Riserva) 10 years; aging in wood.

Marsala DOC disciplinare: Oro and Ambra from Grillo, Catarratto, Ansonica (Inzolia) and Damaschino; Rubino from Perricone (Pignatello), Calabrese (Nero d'Avola) and Nerello Mascalese; mosto cotto is banned in Vergine and in Fine and Superiore Oro and Rubino; sweetness: secco under 40 g/L, semisecco 40-100, dolce over 100.

INAO, AOP Maury: a vin doux naturel made by stopping fermentation around mid-fermentation with 96° wine alcohol (mutage); Grenache Noir is the base of grenat and tuilé; ambré and tuilé are aged oxidatively, sometimes for decades; AOC for vins doux naturels since 1936, dry reds since 2011; black schist soils.

Pineau des Charentes cahier des charges (decree 2011-1453): a vin de liqueur made by muting grape must with AOC Cognac (at least 60% ABV) to 16-22% ABV; must over 170 g/L sugar at mutage; rosé and red at least 12 months aging (8 in oak), white at least 18 months (12 in oak); 'vieux' at least 5 years in wood, 'très vieux' or 'extra vieux' at least 10.

EU Regulation 1308/2013 Annex VII: liqueur wine has an actual alcoholic strength of 15-22% and a total of at least 17.5% (with exceptions), with added neutral grape alcohol (96%+) or wine distillate (52-86%).

VQA Ontario: Late Harvest at least 22° Brix, Select Late Harvest 26°, Special Select Late Harvest 30°, Icewine 35° (picked below -8 °C); Appassimento or Vin de Cure may be used for wines of at least 85% dried grapes.
27 CFR 4.21: dessert wine is grape wine over 14 and not over 24 percent alcohol; 4.24(a)(2): Vermouth and Sake are examples of generic names.
27 CFR 4.24(a)(2): Vermouth and Sake are generic names of geographic origin in U.S. law.
WOSA: Constantia was the origin of the Constantia dessert wines that became famous throughout Europe in the 18th century.

EU Regulation 251/2014 Art. 3(2): an aromatised wine is at least 75% grapevine products by volume, may have added alcohol, colour, must and sweetening, and has an actual strength of at least 14.5% and under 22%, total at least 17.5%.

EU Regulation 251/2014 Annex II: vermouth is aromatised wine with added alcohol whose taste comes from Artemisia; bitter aromatised wine may be called Quinquina (quinine), Bitter vino (gentian) or Americano (wormwood and gentian); egg-based aromatised wine has over 200 g sugar and at least 10 g egg yolk per liter; 'Sangría' as a sales name only for Spain or Portugal; Glühwein is a named aromatised wine-based drink.

BJCP 2021 (Lambic): spontaneously fermented wild ale from in and around Brussels (Senne Valley, Pajottenland); Pilsner malt and unmalted wheat; aged hops (3+ years) used as a preservative; fermented in well-used neutral oak; traditionally served uncarbonated; Faro is lambic sweetened at service.
BJCP 2021 (Gueuze): one-, two- and three-year-old lambics are blended and bottle-conditioned, giving a sparkling beer; 'oude' or 'vieille' marks the most traditional.

BJCP 2021 (Berliner Weisse): low-alcohol Berlin wheat beer with clean lactic sourness from co-fermentation with top-fermenting yeast and lactic acid bacteria; Napoleon's troops called it 'the Champagne of the North' in 1809.
BJCP 2021 (Weissbier): malted wheat is at least half the grist; decoction mash traditional; banana-and-clove weizen yeast; modern Weissbier dates from 1872 when Schneider began its amber version.
BJCP 2021 (Belgian Tripel): popularized by the monastery at Westmalle, first brewed in 1931; most traditional versions have at least 30 IBUs and are very dry.

BJCP 2021 (Irish Stout): Dublin-type stouts use roasted barley and are drier; Guinness began a 'stouter kind of porter' around 1810; Guinness Draught launched in 1959; draught is usually a nitro pour.
BJCP 2021 (English IPA): the East India Company had Samuel Allsopp recreate the beer in 1823 using Burton's sulfate-rich water; the name India Pale Ale wasn't used until around 1830.
BJCP 2021 (American IPA): the first modern American craft version is generally believed to be Anchor Liberty Ale, first brewed in 1975 with whole Cascade hops.

International Trappist Association: an Authentic Trappist Product must be made within the immediate surroundings of the abbey, under the supervision of the monks or nuns, with profits going to the community, solidarity within the Order, or charity.

National Tax Agency labeling standard (Notice No. 8, 1989): eight special designations: Ginjo (≤60% polishing ratio, added brewer's alcohol), Daiginjo (≤50%, alcohol), Junmai (no ratio), Junmai Ginjo (≤60%), Junmai Daiginjo (≤50%), Tokubetsu Junmai (≤60% or special method), Honjozo (≤70%, alcohol), Tokubetsu Honjozo (≤60% or special method); all need koji rice of at least 15%.

National Tax Agency: the 2003 amendment (in force January 1, 2004) removed Junmai's 70% polishing requirement and added the 15% koji-rice minimum; brewer's alcohol for Ginjo and Honjozo is limited to 10% of the white rice weight; a 60% polishing ratio means 40% of the brown rice was removed; table rice is about 92%.
National Tax Agency: ginjo sake's fruity aroma comes from esters such as isoamyl acetate (banana-like) and ethyl caproate (apple-like); sake typically contains 15-16% alcohol.
NRIB guide: the seed mash (shubo or moto) must be highly acidic; kimoto and yamahaimoto grow lactic acid bacteria (about a month); sokujomoto adds brewing-grade lactic acid and saves about two weeks.

NRIB guide: the main mash is built in three steps over four days (one-sixth on day 1 with the shubo, nothing on day 2, two-sixths on day 3, three-sixths on day 4); fermentation takes three to four weeks and reaches about 17-20% alcohol.
NRIB guide: sake is usually pasteurized twice; namazake not at all; nama-chozo-shu once at bottling after maturation; namazume-shu once before maturation; koshu ages at least three years.

EU Regulation 2019/787 Annex I: whisky is distilled at less than 94.8% vol so the distillate keeps the raw materials' aroma and taste, matured at least three years in wooden casks of no more than 700 liters, minimum 40% ABV, only water and plain caramel added; 'single malt' means only malted barley at a single distillery.

EU Regulation 2019/787 Annex I: rum is distilled from fermented cane-sugar molasses, syrup or cane juice at less than 96% vol, minimum 37.5%; brandy (Weinbrand) matures at least one year in oak of 1,000 liters or more, or six months in oak casks under 1,000 liters, minimum 36%.

EU Regulation 2019/787 Annex I: London gin is distilled gin flavoured only by distillation with all natural plant materials, distillate at least 70% ABV, not coloured, no more than 0.1 g/L sweetening, minimum 37.5%; may add 'dry'.

EU Regulation 2019/787 Annex I: liqueur needs at least 100 g/L sweetening (70 g/L for cherry spirit liqueurs, 80 g/L for gentian or wormwood liqueurs) and at least 15% ABV; crème de needs at least 250 g/L; bitter-tasting spirit drink (bitter) at least 15% ABV.

27 CFR 5.143: bourbon, rye, wheat and malt whisky are at least 51% of that grain, distilled at 160 proof or less and stored in charred new oak at 125 proof or less; straight whisky stores at least 2 years; corn whisky is at least 80% corn; whisky is bottled at least 80 proof; 'bourbon' may be used only for whisky distilled and aged in the United States.
27 CFR 5.88: bottled in bond means one kind of spirit, from one distilling season, one distiller and one distillery, stored at least 4 years in wood, and bottled at 100 proof (50% ABV).

27 CFR 5.144: gin must take its main flavor from juniper and be bottled at least 80 proof; only gin made by original distillation or redistillation may be called 'distilled', 'Dry', 'London' or 'Old Tom'.
27 CFR 5.148: agave spirits are at least 51% from Agave; Tequila and Mezcal are distinctive products of Mexico and must be made there under Mexican rules.

27 CFR 5.147: rum is distilled from sugar cane juice, syrup, molasses or other cane by-products at less than 95% ABV and bottled at least 80 proof; Cachaça is rum that is a distinctive product of Brazil.

Scotch Whisky Regulations 2009, reg. 3: Scotch is distilled in Scotland at less than 94.8% ABV, matured only in Scotland in oak casks of no more than 700 liters for at least three years, minimum 40%; Single Malt Scotch is malted barley only, at a single distillery, in pot stills; Blended Malt, Single Grain, Blended Grain and Blended Scotch are the other categories.
Scotch Whisky Regulations 2009, reg. 10: protected localities are Campbeltown and Islay; protected regions are Highland, Lowland and Speyside.

BNIC: VS minimum 2 years, VSOP 4 years, XO 10 years; the mention gives the age of the youngest eau-de-vie in the blend; Cognac is distilled twice in a Charentais still and aged in oak; six crus; 40% minimum ABV.

BNIC: Cognac cannot be sold before at least two years of aging in oak; some terms are reserved for Cognacs aged 14 years or more; the GI specifications were recognized by French decree No. 2015-10 of 7 January 2015.

Court theory guide, Areas of Study for non-wine subjects: distillation techniques (example: continuous or pot still), laws on distillation and number of distillations, aging requirements, label terms and types (example: types of sake or Scotch).

unverified: Madeira: the IVBAM site (vinhomadeira.com) could not be reached, so Madeira facts come from Wine Folly only. Secondary sources disagree on Frasqueira (19 vs 20 years in cask); the chapter follows Wine Folly's 20.
Sherry minimum age: the Sherry Council page says the 3:1 stock rule guarantees at least three years; this was not checked against the current DO regulations, so no general minimum is stated.

Marsala: the disciplinare was read from a copy hosted by AIS (Associazione Italiana Sommelier); its revision date is not shown. A search summary quoted an older text giving 5 years for Superiore Riserva; the copy read says 4.
Pineau des Charentes: the specification read is the 2011 decree version on a secondary host; INAO lists a modification adopted in February 2026 that was not read.
VDN rules for Banyuls, Rivesaltes, Rasteau and Muscat de Beaumes-de-Venise (spirit percentages, hors d'âge and rancio aging) were not read on INAO's site; only the Maury sheet was read.
Chambéry (named by the Court as an aromatized wine) was not found on an official page; left out.
EU regulations were read in their as-adopted text on legislation.gov.uk because EUR-Lex blocked automated reading; later EU amendments were not checked.
Cognac XO moving from 6 to 10 years in 2018 appears in BNIC press materials found by search but not read; only the current 10-year rule is stated.
Sake: the National Tax Agency's English page only summarizes Notice No. 8; the numbers come from the NTA's Japanese summary page.

read.bigIdea: Sparkling law is pressure, presses and time.
read.where: From Level 2 you know the **traditional method** and the 15- and 36-month rules. At Advanced, learn the numbers in Champagne's **cahier des charges** and how the law sorts sparkling wine by **pressure**.

stops.name: The press
stops.text: Each **marc** gives **2,050 L** of **cuvée** and **500 L** of **taille**, kept apart. The legal ceiling is **102 liters per 160 kg**.

stops.name: The grapes
stops.text: Chardonnay, Meunier and Pinot Noir, plus **Arbane**, **Petit Meslier**, **Pinot Blanc** and **Pinot Gris**. **Voltis**, an adaptation grape, is capped at 10% of a blend.

stops.name: The bottle
stops.text: Tirage starts no earlier than **January 1** after harvest; disgorging waits at least **12 months**. Rosé may be a **blend** of white and red wine.

stops.name: The label
stops.text: **RM** grower, **NM** merchant house, **CM** cooperative, **RC** co-op member's own label, **MA** private label. In the U.S., tank-made 'champagne' must say **bulk process**.

read.visualIntro: The law sorts bubbles by pressure:
read.mixup: **RM** grows and makes its own wine. **RC** is a cooperative member selling co-op wine under its own label.
read.sayIt: This is a grower Champagne: the family grew the grapes and made the wine.

read.bigIdea: Age is certified in Jerez and in Gaia alike.
read.where: From Level 2 you know **flor**, the **solera** and the Port families. At Advanced, learn how age gets **certified**, and the rules for each special **category**.

stops.name: VOS and VORS
stops.text: Average age over **20** (VOS) or **30** (VORS) years, judged lot by lot. Only **Amontillado**, **Oloroso**, **Palo Cortado** or **Pedro Ximénez** qualify.

stops.name: Pagos and añadas
stops.text: Since the 2015 map, a **pago** such as **Macharnudo** needs **85%** of its grapes. **Añadas** age as one vintage in casks sealed by the Consejo.

stops.name: Port's mutage
stops.text: About **one part** grape spirit to **four parts** must-wine stops fermentation, leaving sweetness and **19-22%** ABV.

stops.name: Port's specials
stops.text: **LBV**: four to six years in wood; **Vintage**: bottled after two to three years. **Crusted**: three years in bottle; **Colheita**: seven years in cask.

read.sayIt: This is a VORS Oloroso: more than thirty years old on average.

read.bigIdea: Each fortified wine counts its years differently.
read.where: Madeira, Marsala, **vins doux naturels** and **vins de liqueur** all add spirit, but at different moments. Learn each one's **age ladder** and **mutage**.

stops.name: Madeira
stops.text: **Rainwater** (3 years), then **5, 10, 15, 20+ years**. **Colheita** is one vintage, 5 years; **Frasqueira** is one vintage, **20 years** in **canteiro**.

stops.name: Marsala
stops.text: **Fine** 1 year, **Superiore** 2, **Superiore Riserva** 4, **Vergine** 5, **Vergine Stravecchio** 10. **Oro** and **Ambra** are white grapes; **Rubino** is red. No **mosto cotto** in Vergine.

stops.name: Vin doux naturel
stops.text: Fermentation is stopped midway with **96%** grape spirit. **Grenache Noir** makes the **grenat** and **tuilé**; ambré and tuilé age oxidatively.

stops.name: Vin de liqueur
stops.text: Grape must muted with **Cognac** to **16-22%**. White ages 18 months (12 in oak); 'vieux' needs 5 years in wood.

read.visualIntro: When the spirit goes in decides the name:
read.mixup: A **VDN** starts fermenting before it is muted. A **VDL** like Pineau is must muted with spirit.
read.sayIt: Pineau des Charentes: fresh grape juice and Cognac, aged in oak.

read.bigIdea: Sweet comes from ripeness, drying, or a spice box.
read.where: Sweet wines get their sugar from the vine, from **drying**, from noble rot or from fortifying. **Aromatized wines** start as wine and add botanicals, sugar and often alcohol.

stops.name: Left on the vine
stops.text: **Late Harvest** 22° Brix, **Select** 26°, **Special Select** 30°, **Icewine** 35° and picked below -8 °C.

stops.name: Dried after picking
stops.text: VQA's **Appassimento** needs 85% dried grapes. **Pedro Ximénez** is sun-dried (**asoleo**), then muted with wine alcohol.

stops.name: Aromatized wine
stops.text: At least **75% wine**, **14.5%** to under **22%** ABV. **Vermouth** gets its taste from **Artemisia**, with alcohol added.

stops.name: The bitter family
stops.text: **Quinquina** is quinine; **Bitter vino** is gentian; **Americano** is wormwood and gentian. **Sangría** belongs to Spain and Portugal.

read.visualIntro: The EU names aromatized wines by their flavor:
read.sayIt: Vermouth is wine with botanicals and a little added spirit.

read.bigIdea: Beer is read by place; sake by polishing.
read.where: From Level 2 you know malt, hops and yeast, and the basic sake grades. At Advanced, tie each **classic beer** to its place and method, and learn the **sake law** behind the label.

stops.name: Wild and sour
stops.text: **Lambic** ferments spontaneously in well-used oak; **gueuze** blends one-, two- and three-year-old lambic. **Berliner Weisse** sours with **lactic bacteria**.

stops.name: Monks and wheat
stops.text: **Westmalle** popularized the **Tripel** in 1931. **Weissbier** is at least half malted wheat, with banana-and-clove yeast.

stops.name: Sake law
stops.text: **Honjozo** 70% or less, **Ginjo** 60%, **Daiginjo** 50%. **Junmai** has no polishing minimum since 2004. Added alcohol is capped at **10%** of the rice weight.

stops.name: Sake making
stops.text: The seed mash is **kimoto**, **yamahai** or **sokujo**. The main mash goes in over **four days** in **three steps**. **Namazake** is never pasteurized.

read.mixup: **Namazake** is never pasteurized. **Nama-chozo** is pasteurized once, at bottling.
read.sayIt: Junmai Daiginjo: rice milled to half or less, and no added alcohol.

read.bigIdea: Distill low for flavor, then age by the law.
read.where: The Court asks about **distillation** (pot or continuous, how many times), **aging laws** and **label terms**. The rules are written so the spirit keeps the taste of its **raw material**.

stops.name: Distillation strength
stops.text: EU and Scotch whisky stay under **94.8%** ABV; bourbon under **160 proof**. **Single Malt Scotch** must use **pot stills**; **Cognac** is distilled **twice** in a Charentais still.

stops.name: Whisky aging
stops.text: **Scotch**: 3 years in oak of **700 L** or less. **Straight** whiskey: 2 years in charred new oak. **Bottled in bond**: 4 years, **100 proof**.

stops.name: Brandy aging
stops.text: EU **brandy**: 1 year in big oak or **6 months** in casks under 1,000 L. **Cognac**: **VS** 2, **VSOP** 4, **XO** 10 years, counting the youngest spirit.

stops.name: Aperitifs and digestifs
stops.text: **Vermouth**: 75%+ wine; **bitter**: 15% ABV or more. **Liqueur**: 100 g/L sugar; **crème de**: 250 g/L. **London gin**: flavored only by distillation.

read.mixup: **Single Malt** Scotch is one distillery, malted barley, pot stills. **Blended Malt** mixes single malts from more than one distillery.
read.sayIt: An XO Cognac: the youngest brandy in it is at least ten years old.
